newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle 1996 margin on sales up to 5.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nestle 1996 margin on sales up to 5.6 pct.

text.p: Nestle SA said its margin on sales rose to 5.6 percent in 1996 from 5.2 percent in 1995.

The operating margin was unchanged at 9.7 percent, even though the group increased its advertising and promotional spending to support the launch of new products and increase market share, it said in a statement on 1996 results.

Restructuring costs also rose, mainly as a consequence of measures taken to improve competitiveness in western Europe. "They remain substantially below the level reached in the years before 1995," it said without giving details.

"As the result of the appreciation of foreign currencies vis a vis the Swiss franc, the net financial debt of the group increased from 6.3 billion to 6.8 billion francs, as the overwhelming part of the financial debt of the group is contracted in foreign currencies," it said.

"In today's meeting the board of directors decided to propose to the general meeting that the dividend be raised from 26.50 francs to 30 francs per share. The pay-out ratio will consequently amount to 34.7 percent of the profit per share."
If shareholders approve, dividends will be payable from June 11. No transfer of shares affecting voting rights will be registered between May 16 and the day of the general meeting.
The board will propose that Peter Brabeck-Letmathe -- executive vice president and sete to replace chairman Helmut Maucer as chief executive in June -- be elected as a director.
